column5: Description

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Stone Flow
Aspect: 3 Earth + 1 Water
Description: This spell infuses targeted piece/volume of rock in a few seconds of focus. Infused pieces of stone can be shaped like clay by the user's hand or even be made flow akin to a liquid small distance away by user's will. When a spell stops working after some time or when it is dispelled, the stone turns back solid and keeps its new shape. This spell works better at softer rocks: harder the rock - more time it takes to infuse and harder it is to mold.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Glass Staining
Aspect: 1 Earth + 1 Light
Description: This spell affects a targeted piece or volume of glass. It alters the internal crystalline structure of the glass to permanently change its color by introducing specific tendencies toward the refraction and absorption of light within the material. It can be used to make a piece of glass red, green, or any relatively simple shade the caster desires. It can also make glass frosted, more opaque, or even produce simple multicolored patterns. However, this spell depends heavily on the skill of the caster. It is easy to simply make glass redder, but much harder to achieve a specific hue or introduce a precise pattern. It takes considerable practice to master.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Concrete Setting
Aspect: 1 Earth + 1 Order
Description: This spell targets mortar, cement, or similar binding materials. It accelerates and refines the setting process, meaning the material turns solid more quickly and with fewer internal imperfections than it would naturally. When the spell takes effect, it produces a small burst of infrared light and a modest amount of waste heat.

You've learned a new enchantment!

Name: Cooling Surface Charm
Aspect: 3 Air + 1 Order + 1 Water
Description: This enchantment can be applied to a small surface. It persists for a few years, but gradually deteriorates over time and can be broken by severely damaging the enchanted object. When the surface bearing this charm moves through air, it causes the gas in contact with it to cool down by one or two degrees Celsius. The charm cannot bring temperatures lower than 19 degrees Celsius, but it is quite good to have cast on fan blades on a hot day.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Root-Weave Compaction
Aspect: 2 Earth + 2 Life + 1 Water
Description: The caster places their palms flat on bare soil and hums at a low frequency. Over the course of a minute, the spell encourages the dormant seeds and fungal mycelium within the soil to grow at an accelerated, controlled rate. The roots intertwine into a dense, living mat while simultaneously absorbing ambient moisture to swell and fill every void. The result is a section of ground that becomes as hard and load-bearing as packed gravel, but remains permeable to water. The effect is permanent, as the root-mat continues to live and self-repair, though it requires annual "re-tuning" to prevent overgrowth or death.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Lumicrete Mixture
Aspect: 3 Light + 1 Earth
Description: A dry mortar or concrete powder is piled up and the caster speaks a sustained, resonant word over it. The powder glows faintly for a few moments and then goes dark. When mixed with water and poured, the setting process is accelerated to completion in under an hour (instead of days). More importantly, the crystalline structure of the cured material aligns in such a way that it "stores" ambient light. During the day, the surface absorbs sunlight; at night, it emits a soft, moon-like glow equivalent to a well-lit corridor for up to eight hours. It does not produce heat.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Chord of True Level
Aspect: 2 Space + 1 Order
Description: The caster snaps a length of ordinary twine or rope taut between two stakes. They then whisper the spell and flick the twine. A barely-visible ripple of blue-white light travels along the cord, and the twine goes unnaturally rigid. For the next hour, the twine is magically anchored to the planet's gravitational core, making it a perfectly horizontal and vibration-less reference line. This is the surveyor's best friend, used to lay perfectly straight aqueduct channels, set door frames, and pour flawless floors. The twine can be moved and re-anchored, but each re-setting requires a new casting.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Slow-Glass Annealing
Aspect: 2 Fire + 2 Earth + 1 Time
Description: This spell is cast over a kiln or a sand-smelter right as the molten silica is poured into its molds. Instead of flash-cooling, the spell extends the cooling process over a period of several days, but does so internally, eliminating all thermal stress and micro-fractures. The resulting glass panes are cheap to produce (no fuel for slow cooling ovens) and have the tensile strength of wrought iron. Used to create massive, flawless windows for public buildings, greenhouse panels, and translucent floor-tiles for upper-story walkways.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Draft-Ward Seal
Aspect: 2 Air + 1 Order
Description: The caster traces the outline of a door, window, or city-gate with their finger, leaving a faint silver tracing. The spell doesn't stop airflow completely, but it equalizes air pressure and temperature between the inside and outside by "slowing" the chaotic movement of air particles to a gentle, laminar flow. Ward deteriorates over a few weeks and can be disrupted.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Miracle of Healing (Impure Regeneration) 
Aspect: 1 Light + 1 Healing + 1 Life
Description: This spell produces a small amount of healing light, which can be infused into a living target or projected in a direction to cause rapid regeneration. The spell takes biomass from various tissues in the body in such a way as to cause the least amount of damage, and uses this biomass to heal a variety of wounds. It can even restore eyesight lost due to injury, regenerate parts of damaged organs, and even grow new limbs. However, more intensive effects require prolonged use of the spell or repeated applications. It takes a full week of uninterrupted healing light to grow a new arm - though this time can be broken down into shorter sessions.

Historical Note: This spell was discovered and used by priests of an ancient eastern civilization, who believed it was a revelation from their god of healing. It was used extensively after its discovery, causing the early empire to become a powerful regional force, conquer many neighbors, and elevate the social status of the healing god's priests to great heights. 

Unfortunately (unknown to anyone at the time) the spell carried a terrible hidden cost. Using the Miracle of Healing increased the chances of cancer in subsequent years, and also increased the likelihood of genetic disorders in the offspring of those affected by the healing light. The effect was cumulative: those who bathed in the light more frequently suffered worse consequences later. This caused the civilization to collapse after a few generations.

That said, the spell can still be used safely in moderation. A single application to save a friend from blood loss (transforming a small amount of fat into blood) carries only a tiny increase in cancer risk, far outweighed by the immediate benefit. The danger lies in repeated exposure, especially to the intense regeneration required for major wounds, limbs, or organs.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Heat Metal
Aspect: 3 Fire + 1 Metal
Description: This spell produces a short cone of red light. When this light strikes a targeted piece of metal, it heats the metal quickly and evenly throughout its entire volume. The spell can heat metal up to 1,344 degrees Celsius. However, different metals, alloys, and compositions require fine-tuning of the spell. 

Heating iron and copper requires very different compositions of the spell, while heating one type of steel versus another introduces small changes that must be accounted for. Mastering this spell requires extensive practice and experimentation with different metals. If tuned wrong it doesn’t work or works only partially.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Carve Wood
Aspect: 3 Wood + 1 Force
Description: This spell infuses a piece of wood with a touch and produces a cutting surface that intersects the volume of the material. The cut can be made rough or smooth, and the geometry of the surface can vary: a simple plane passing through the volume, a cut that does not go all the way through, a wavy surface, or even one with holes. It cannot, however, produce a completely closed surface. 

After the cutting surface is placed inside the volume of the wood, the caster activates it, causing the cut to follow the surface's geometry through the material they are touching. It works quicker and easier on less dense types of wood.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Wave of Erosion
Aspect: 3 Earth + 1 Chaos
Description: This spell produces a "wave" that travels through stone or other minerals of a similar nature from the point of contact. Each wave loosens the integrity of the material, breaks it down, and eventually turns it into fine dust of evenly redistributed mineral components. The finer the end result, the longer and more difficult it is to achieve. 

It is relatively easy to break down a stone into smaller shards (taking only a few seconds), but much harder and more time-consuming to turn sand into dust (taking around an hour). The spell works best on smaller volumes; the wave has limited capacity to travel through material and becomes weaker the further it gets from the point of contact. Denser materials with more complex compositions are more resistant to the spell. It does not affect metals.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Stone-Bond Welding
Aspect: 2 Earth + 1 Fire + 1 Order
Description: This spell fuses two pieces of stone or ceramics together at their contact surfaces, effectively "welding" them into a single continuous mass. The caster presses the two pieces together and channels the spell through the joint, causing the stone at the interface to soften, flow, and re-crystallize as a seamless bond. The resulting joint is as strong as the surrounding stone, with no visible seam. The spell works best on similar stone types and requires careful preparation of the surfaces: they must be clean, dry, and closely matched.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Become Entropy
Aspect: 1 Chaos
Description: Choose a point on your body from which the spell will be cast. From this point, everything within a few meters in a direction of your choice will suddenly have its entropy heightened: things will break down, mix, and reach thermal equilibrium over a few seconds. In practical terms: things disintegrate. 

However, you are inevitably caught at the edge of the spell's volume of effect. If you cast it from your fingertips in a forward direction, your hand will also succumb to entropy. The spell is more effective against targets of lesser density, and certain materials or composites are more resistant to it than others.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Scissors Fingers
Aspect: 2 Force + 1 Order + 1 Semblance
Description: This spell is cast and sustained on your fingers. Make a scissors gesture and activate the spell. It will create a thin metallic glint on the inner sides of your fingers. You can now use this gesture as actual sharp scissors to cut soft materials such as paper, thin leather, cardboard, fabric, and similar items. This spell does not affect living tissues.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Thread-Finger
Aspect: 1 Semblance + 1 Force
Description: The caster's fingertip extrudes a thin, temporary filament of magical force that acts like thread. It can be used to sew, stitch, or bind materials together, or to tie small knots. The thread has the tensile strength of strong cotton and lasts for several hours before dissolving harmlessly. Useful for field repairs or any situation where needle and thread are unavailable.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Steady Hand
Aspect: 2 Order + 1 Semblance + 1 Lore
Description: This spell creates a temporary visual guide (a faint glowing line or grid) that overlays the caster's field of vision, helping them cut, draw, or place objects with perfect alignment. It lasts as long as the caster maintains concentration. Used by masons, carpenters, scribes, and artists.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Measuring Eye
Aspect: 1 Order + 1 Light + 2 Lore
Description: The caster can gauge the exact dimensions (length, width, depth) of any object within their line of sight, up to a distance of fifty meters. The information appears in their mind as precise measurements. However, the caster must already understand what they are measuring and how to measure it, as well as the units they are using. 

If you do not know how to measure something by hand, or what you are measuring, the spell will not work, or will only work partially. Used by surveyors, architects, carpenters, and tailors.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Marker's Trace
Aspect: 1 Order + 1 Semblance + 1 Light
Description: The caster traces a finger along a surface, leaving a faint glowing line that marks a specific measurement or cut line. The line persists for a few minutes (without sustaining) before fading, allowing the caster to mark multiple points or cut lines without needing chalk, pencil, or string.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Needle Finger
Aspect: 2 Force + 1 Semblance
Description: This spell is cast and sustained on your fingertip. Make a pointing gesture with one finger and cast the spell. It will create a thin metallic glint extending a few millimeters from the tip of your finger. You can now use this gesture as an actual sharp needle point, allowing you to make holes in soft materials like thin leather, paper, fabric, cardboard, and similar items. 

You can control the diameter and depth of the puncture within certain limits (up to four millimeters deep and two millimeters wide). It takes more force and time to puncture harder or denser materials, or to make a larger hole. This spell does not affect living tissues.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Gather Moisture
Aspect: 2 Water + 1 Air
Description: This spell is used to gather and concentrate moisture from the volume of air around the caster (up to a maximum radius of around four meters). It does not work through walls. The spell condenses water vapor into liquid form and produces a ball of water at the focus center of the spell. It cannot lower the humidity of the air around further than 7.2%.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Crystallization
Aspect: 1 Water + 1 Order + 1 Transformation
Description: This spell rapidly causes a targeted liquid to crystallize and become solid. It does not require contact, but proximity is needed, and crystallization starts from the closest point to the caster. The spell does not lower the temperature of the liquid - it merely makes it solid and keeps it that way for a time, or while the spell is sustained by the caster. 

For example, it can turn boiling water into ice and keep it in that state for a few hours (or while actively sustained), while preserving its boiling hot temperature. Different kinds of liquids require different fine-tuning of the spell; some liquids are easier to affect than others. When the spell duration ends, the targeted substance returns to its normal state.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Evaporation
Aspect: 1 Water + 1 Chaos + 1 Transformation
Description: This spell rapidly causes a targeted liquid to evaporate and become a gas. It does not require contact, but proximity is needed, and evaporation starts from the closest point to the caster. The spell does not change the temperature of the liquid - it merely makes it gaseous and keeps it that way for a time, or while the spell is sustained by the caster. 

For example, it can turn cold water into vapor and keep it in that state for a few hours (or while actively sustained), while preserving its freezing cold temperature. Different kinds of liquids require different fine-tuning of the spell; some liquids are easier to affect than others. When the spell duration ends, the targeted substance returns to its normal state.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Bubble Telekinesis
Aspect: 2 Force + 1 Air
Description: This spell creates a barely visible bubble that can be used to envelop and lift objects. Things moved this way become buoyant inside the bubble and will follow it as it moves. This spell can lift and move very heavy objects, but it does so slowly. Trying to push it to move more quickly might separate the object from the bubble enveloping it. This spell can move loose materials like sand, gravel, or even liquids, but it may lose some small pieces while moving such materials.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Film Telekinesis
Aspect: 2 Force + 1 Earth
Description: This spell creates a barely visible, glinting film on the surface of an object, which envelops and presses slightly on it. Objects follow the movement of the film that envelops them. The caster must be close to apply the film, but once applied, they can move the object further away, fix it relative to certain places, or even move several independently. It can move objects rather quickly and in a decently precise manner. However, it cannot handle very heavy objects; overly complicated surfaces make the spell weaker; and it works only on solid items.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Push Telekinesis
Aspect: 1 Force + 1 Space
Description: This spell makes objects float (as if without gravity) and can apply a vector of acceleration to the center of mass of the affected item. It has a maximum speed it can accelerate an object toward, but on the other hand, it can be used to slow down already moving objects (if one can focus on them). This spell is more powerful and more precise the closer it is to the caster (maximum radius of ten meters). Heavier objects accelerate more slowly with this spell. It can be used to make loose materials and liquids float, but it cannot apply vector acceleration to them.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Hand Projection
Aspect: 1 Force + 1 Air + 1 Semblance + 1 Mind
Description: This spell creates projections (resembling ghosts or holograms) of the user's hands, which they can move around and use to hold, catch, or manipulate objects. The spell provides feedback, feeling like moving your own hands and touching something. These hands are not very strong, and it is difficult to have more than two doing anything complex at a time. 

However, they can be used to hold things, perform simple repetitive movements, or similar tasks. This spell depends heavily on the user's skill and dexterity: if the user cannot write neatly, the hands they create will not write neatly either.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Psychokinesis
Aspect: 1 Mind + 2 Force + 1 Aether
Description: This spell targets the soul of a living being and moves it, causing the body to follow. It allows the caster to hold, reposition, or move living targets. A target who is awake and in full possession of their will can resist the spell's effect or even assist it, making the spell easier to cast on willing subjects. The spell can move the target evenly - with or without the acceleration-induced G-load that would normally accompany such movement. 

The spell can be sustained, allowing the caster to hold a target in place, suspend them mid-air, or slowly lower them to safety. However, maintaining the spell on an unwilling target is exhausting and requires constant mental effort. So its easier to just suddenly push.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Light Telekinesis
Aspect: 1 Light + 2 Force + 1 Order
Description: This spell produces a ray of light effect (although not as fast as actual light). When this ray strikes a separate object, it causes the target to glow faintly in outline and allows the caster to move the object by manipulating the beam of light connecting them. The spell can be used to rotate objects, drag them closer, or push them further away, or generally move them around.

However, the ray connecting the caster and the target can be disrupted by other objects passing between them. The beam will attempt to bend and evade obstacles intersecting its path, but it has limitations: too many obstacles, rapidly moving objects, or solid barriers can break the connection entirely. Intersecting objects will become a new target or disrupt the spell completely. The beam also has a maximum effective range of about thirty meters, beyond which it dissipates.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Radiant Grasp
Aspect: 1 Light + 1 Force + 1 Air
Description: Instead of a single beam, this spell produces a diffuse cone of glowing light. Everything within the cone is lightly grasped, allowing the caster to push or pull multiple objects at once. Though with less individual control and strength than Light Telekinesis. Useful for clearing debris, scattering projectiles, or moving a group of small objects. The cone loses strength with distance and is easily blocked.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Create Water
Aspect: 1 Water + 1 Creation
Description: This spell allows the caster to create a small amount of pure water per casting. It can produce up to 0.909 liters of water at a time, in the form of a simple shape, which is soon after creation affected by gravity. This water contains no impurities - it is perfectly distilled and permanent. The temperature of the water can vary between 4 and 66 degrees Celsius, and this can be tuned by the caster.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Create Salt
Aspect: 1 Creation + 1 Earth
Description: This spell allows the caster to create a piece of pure, permanent salt (either as one chunk or as several smaller pieces) in a simple shape, which soon after creation is affected by gravity and falls. It can create a maximum of 0.314 kilograms of salt per casting.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Exhumation
Aspect: 2 Earth + 1 Death
Description: This spell causes all dead bodies within a targeted volume of earth to be pushed upward and reach the surface. It separates dead bodies from the earth, like wood floating to the surface of water. The caster does not need to know a body is present - simply target a volume of earth beneath you and watch as all carcasses are pushed to the surface without leaving any holes (only some slightly disturbed soil).

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Grave-Seal
Aspect: 2 Earth + 1 Death + 1 Order
Description: This spell is cast upon a burial site to prevent Exhumation from working. It binds the dead to their resting place, making them "heavier" than the earth around them. Corpses under Grave-Seal cannot be raised, floated, or disturbed by magical means. Used by temples, families, and governments to protect the sanctity of graves. Need to be reapplied every few months.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Bone-Whisper
Aspect: 1 Death + 1 Mind + 1 Aether
Description: This spell allows the caster to receive vague impressions from a corpse or skeleton: fragments of memory, emotion, or sensation from the moment of death. The older the corpse, the fainter the impressions.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Press Plastic
Aspect: 4 Plastic + 1 Transformation
Description: This spell allows the caster to target a piece of plastic they are touching and infuse it with the spell over the course of a few seconds. The caster then chooses a shape and activates the spell, causing the plastic to reshape itself into the desired form with a slight pop, as if it had been pressed into its new shape. It can produce some details and relatively complex shapes, but not overly so. The spell requires attuning to different kinds of plastics and works more easily on some than on others.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Plastic-Bond
Aspect: 2 Plastic + 1 Earth
Description: This spell fuses two pieces of plastic together at their contact surfaces, effectively "welding" them into a single piece. The fusion is as strong as the surrounding plastic. Used for repairing broken items, joining pieces, or creating larger structures from smaller components.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Polishing Touch
Aspect: 3 Transformation + 1 Order + 1 Earth
Description: This spell allows the caster to polish solid surfaces with their palms. The user can control how smooth they want the surface to be with each movement of their palm along the surface. Harder and denser surfaces require more time and more passes to polish. This spell can polish materials as hard as certain cast iron alloys, though doing so takes a long time and a great deal of "scrubbing."

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Roughening Touch
Aspect: 3 Transformation + 1 Chaos + 1 Earth
Description: This spell is the opposite of Polishing Touch. It allows the caster to roughen solid surfaces with their palms. The user can control how rough they want the surface to be with each movement of their palm along the surface. Harder and denser surfaces require more time and more passes to roughen. This spell can roughen materials as hard as certain cast iron alloys, though doing so takes a very long time and a great deal of "scrubbing." The resulting texture can range from a fine, matte finish (barely different from polished) to a coarse, abrasive surface like sandpaper, depending on the caster's intent and effort.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Edge-Sharpening
Aspect: 2 Transformation + 1 Order + 1 Force
Description: This spell allows the caster to sharpen the edge of a blade or tool with their thumb. The user can control the angle and fineness of the edge with each pass of their thumb along the blade. Harder materials take more passes and it cannot affect things harder than glass. The spell cannot create an edge from a dull surface - it only refines an existing edge. It works worse, if the edge is less defined.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Healing Touch
Aspect: 3 Healing + 1 Life
Description: This spell allows the caster to accelerate scabbing on a touched wound and stop mild bleeding. It requires more time to deal with deeper and larger wounds. It aids natural healing but does not cause regeneration or rapid tissue repair - it merely makes the wound more protected and ready to heal, while preventing the immediate danger of bleeding out.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Tree Grafting
Aspect: 3 Wood + 1 Healing + 1 Life
Description: This spell allows the caster to graft one type of wood to another. It causes quick fusion and integration of a new branch at the point of contact and slightly accelerates natural growth. It can only target trees and woody plants.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Time Keeping
Aspect: 1 Order + 1 Time + 2 Lore
Description: This spell functions the same as Measuring Eye, but for measuring how much time has passed since the spell was activated. The caster activates the spell and, upon focusing on it later, receives a precise measurement of the elapsed duration. The information appears in their mind as a clear sense of time passed - down to the second. 

However, as with Measuring Eye, the caster must already understand the units they are measuring in and have a conceptual grasp of timekeeping. If you do not understand hours, minutes, or seconds, the spell will not work - or will only work partially, perhaps giving you a vague sense of "long" or "short" rather than precise numbers.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Sun-Reading
Aspect: 1 Light + 1 Time + 2 Lore
Description: This spell tells the caster the current time of day based on the position of the sun (or stars, at night). The information appears in their mind as a precise time, but only if they have a clear view of the sky and understand the local timekeeping system. In overcast conditions the spell less accurate, and indoors - the spell fails. Effectively a magical sundial that works even without a physical sundial.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Weight Sense
Aspect: 1 Space + 2 Lore + 1 Earth
Description: This spell allows the caster to gauge the exact weight or mass of an object they are touching or can see within a short distance. The information appears in their mind as a precise weight in the units they understand. Used by merchants, alchemists, cooks, and anyone who needs to measure quantities.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Food Duplication
Aspect: 3 Creation + 2 Semblance + 1 Transformation
Description: This spell allows the caster to target a portion of food no larger than 1.344 liters in volume and no heavier than 3.5 kilograms. The spell creates a duplicate of the targeted dish nearby, but the duplicate has only 50% of the nutritional value of the original.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Death Ray
Aspect: 1 Light + 2 Death + 1 Hurt
Description: This spell produces a ray of light that flies at supersonic speed and possesses penetrative properties similar to an X-ray beam. When it strikes living tissue, it causes death and decomposition from the point of contact. At full power, a single good hit from this spell is enough to kill a quarter of the cells in an average human by volume, and causing a sixth to decompose into simple organic sludge.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Vitality Ward
Aspect: 3 Life + 1 Protection + 1 Light
Description: This spell creates a faint shimmering barrier around the caster that absorbs incoming attacks specifically targeting life force or ones using death magic. It protects against spells like Death Ray by dissipating their Death and Hurt aspects before they reach the caster's tissue. The ward is fragile, capable of absorbing only one or two powerful attacks before collapsing. It glows with a warm, golden light when hit and that dims as it weakens.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Suffer!
Aspect: 3 Hurt + 1 Mind + 1 Aether
Description: This spell produces a small, sickly-looking orb that flies as quickly as an arrow and can penetrate solid objects with force, though not much (it can pierce a thin steel barrier). When it strikes a living creature, it triggers a sensation of pain and disgust. This sensation is the most painful thing the target has ever experienced, but with a slight edge to it (about 1.5% more intense). 

This information is taken from their soul and projected onto their body. The relative nature of the sensation means the spell always creates a new peak of suffering for the target, meaning subsequent hits will be slightly worse than the last.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Enrich Soil
Aspect: 2 Earth + 1 Creation + 1 Life
Description: This spell targets a volume of soil (no more than five cubic meters at a time) and, over the course of ten minutes, enriches it with beneficial elements, making it more fertile. However, it uses substances already present in the soil and duplicates them in small quantities. It is possible for the soil to be too diminished in one or all aspects for the spell to work effectively or not at all.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Dust Banishment
Aspect: 1 Destruction + 2 Earth
Description: This spell targets dust and small debris on surfaces, making them instantly vanish without a trace and leaving a clean surface behind. It cannot target stains that are strongly stuck to the surface, and it may require several castings if there is a significant amount of dust. If the amount is too great, the spell will not work at all - it cannot be used to vanish a pile of dust. The spell works better on some types of dust and worse on others.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Blemish Erasure
Aspect: 1 Destruction + 1 Water + 1 Order
Description: This spell targets stains and spots on surfaces, breaking them down molecule by molecule until they vanish. Unlike Dust Banishment, it can handle stuck-on stains, but it requires the caster to understand the nature of the stain (oil, wine, blood, etc.) and takes longer to work. Cannot be used on living tissue.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Fresh Scent
Aspect: 1 Air + 1 Semblance + 1 Mind
Description: This spell creates a pleasant, clean scent in a targeted area - subtle and refreshing rather than perfumed. The scent fades after a few hours. Often used in conjunction with Dust Banishment to create a feeling of cleanliness. The exact scent can vary based on the caster's intention (fresh linen, mountain air, citrus, etc.).

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Banishment
Aspect: 2 Destruction + 1 Chaos + 1 Order
Description: This spell causes all matter and energy in a small targeted radius (up to six inches) to vanish without a trace. The spell has a unique sound and the effect of a black orb appearing in the targeted area for just a moment, leaving behind a cleanly cut-out volume. It requires a second to target, and if miscast, the sphere of annihilation will appear somewhere within the caster's body.

You've learned a new ritual!

Name: The Sun Calling
Aspect: 1 Light + 3 Fire + 2 Air + 1 Space
Description: This is a complicated ritual that usually takes a few days to complete and requires rare materials to be consumed. The end result of a successful ritual is a dark, obsidian-like shape that resembles an egg. When the object is accelerated, it produces a dim warm glow. 

When broken or activated by magic, the object begins to glow: red → yellow → white → blue... and then it transforms into a miniature sun, emulating fusion processes within, causing a massive explosion (approximately one-tenth of a kiloton). If the ritual is disturbed, it either fails and fizzles out, or it causes a much smaller explosion without the "phoenix egg" being formed.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: The Moon Calling
Aspect: 1 Water + 3 Aether + 2 Mind + 1 Space
Description: This is a complicated ritual that usually takes a few days to complete and requires rare materials to be consumed. The end result of a successful ritual is a pearl-like shape with a blueish iridescent tint. When the object is accelerated, it becomes dimmer and darker. When broken or activated by magic, the pearl plants a vivid vision and experience into the minds of everyone caught in the produced wave of silver light (approximately 100 meters radius). 

The nature of the mental add-on is decided when the ritual is performed, and the effect irreversibly alters the personality and beliefs of those caught in it. If the ritual is disturbed, it either fails and fizzles out, or it causes a much smaller and less predictable "wave of madness" to be released.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Dry Bones

Description: This spell targets a dead body (or parts of one) and rapidly draws out all remaining moisture, leaving the tissue dried and preserved. Description: This spell targets a living creature. It creates a thin, barely visible tether between the caster and the target, and sends a request into the target's soul. Name: Internal Abacus

Description: This spell creates a temporary partition in the caster's mind that functions like a calculator. The user can enter various mathematical operations they understand how to perform, and the Internal Abacus will quickly provide the solution.

Name: Penance
Aspect: 1 Hurt + 1 Healing
Description: This spell causes the caster themselves to receive painful, but temporary and mostly illusory, wounds. The caster can control how much pain they experience and for how long - up to around an hour or until they lose consciousness.

Description: Make a chopping gesture with your hand. Around your palm and extending some distance away from it (approximately five inches from the fingertips), a burning-like crimson aura will appear, which sounds like a knife being sharpened when moved through the air. Aspect: 3 Hurt + 1 Force + 1 Semblance

Name: Fall!

Description: This spell is channeled through a gesture - a downward pointing of the finger. Description: This spell is cast once to linger on the caster's body for some time (up to 44 minutes). Description: This spell slightly elongates the user's nails, making them sharp like claws and distinctly red. It can be channeled, sustained, or cast for a duration (up to three minutes). Description: This spell can be channeled, sustained, or cast for a duration (up to 33 minutes). It affects all of the user's hair, turning it into a ginger-colored reactive shield. Name: Wound Patch

Name: Epinephrine Charm

Name: Immune Fortification

Aspect: 2 Life + 1 Lightning
Description: This spell produces a barely visible blue aura around the caster's hand. This aura can be used to force muscles to relax and prevent movement in the area by touch. Alternatively, the spell can be channeled into the target for more general paralysis and relaxation, or to make the effect stick for a time (up to an hour).

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Sterile Field
Aspect: 2 Protection + 1 Life + 1 Air +1 Earth 
Description: This spell creates a temporary, invisible barrier around a targeted area (such as a wound, a surgical site, or a medical instrument) that repels bacteria, viruses, and other contaminants. The field lasts for several hours or until deliberately dismissed. Used in field medicine to prevent infection when sterile conditions cannot be guaranteed. It is highly efficient, but not perfect.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Muscle Relaxant
Aspect: 2 Life + 1 Water + 1 Healing
Description: A gentler variant of Paralytic Touch that reduces muscle tension without causing full paralysis. The target remains mobile but feels relaxed and loose, with reduced strength and reflexes. Useful for treating spasms, anxiety, or preparing a patient for physical therapy.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Slicing Curse
Aspect: 2 Hurt + 1 Curse + 1 Force
Description: A sibling of the Slicing Spell. This curse manifests as a semi-transparent, dark greenish-yellow projectile shaped like a thin crescent with a jagged edge. When it strikes a creature, it leaves an ugly cut and causes temporary severe bleeding. It can penetrate thin armor, but its intended target is living flesh.

Wounds left by this curse heal several times slower, bleed more profusely, and leave ugly scars that tend to ache, reopen, and even bleed again on occasion. Like all curses, it resists being reversed.

>Requires Spell: Slicing Spell

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Sweating Sickness
Aspect: 2 Life + 1 Fire + 1 Curse
Description: This curse appears as a streak of ugly flame and carries a faint scent of sweat. When it strikes a target, it induces a high (but not deadly) fever that lasts for several hours. From that point on, the fever will return and subside periodically. Sometimes it lasts a few hours, sometimes a full day. It may strike once a month or several times a week. In the long run, this will surely wear down the victim's body and spirit unless the curse is lifted or countered somehow.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Snap & Seal
Aspect: 1 Curse + 1 Hurt + 1 Force + 1 Heal
Description: This curse appears as a barely visible slab of black and white, accompanied by a wet snapping sound - similar to the Bone Breaker spell. It is a projectile that can pass through low-density obstacles and living tissue, gradually losing power until stopped.

When it strikes bone, it interacts like fast-moving metallic material, typically fracturing or breaking it. The bone then instantly heals, but in the wrong, fractured state. The curse actively resists any attempt to correct the mishealed bone.

>Requires Spell: Bone Breaker

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Hurting
Aspect: 1 Hurt
Description: Creates a semi-transparent, head-sized orb of flowing red and violet swirls. It moves as quickly as a stone thrown from a sling. When the orb hits, it creates a heavy impact and pushes the target away. The effect is much stronger against living things - dramatically so. It can leave literal cylindrical holes in a target, like a cannonball. However, it pops soon after impact.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Drubbing
Aspect: 1 Hurt
Description: This spell produces a swarm (12 to 43) of small orbs, which look like semi-transparent ball bearings filled with red and violet swirls. They flow together like a swarm of flies and can be sustained by the caster as a relentless wave of newly produced orbs, and even slightly controlled. Each one creates a small impact on contact with inanimate things and punches like a fist on contact with a creature. They pop on impact.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Carnage
Aspect: 2 Hurt + 1 Chaos
Description: This is a bolt-quick streak of yellow-crimson color. When it hits a creature, it causes tissues around the zone of impact to explode like a bloody, gory balloon. It can be blocked by thick enough physical barriers and it simply punches them instead. The volume it explodes can be tuned within certain limits (from exploding a finger, to popping half the torso of tissue).

You've learned two new martial techniques!

Name: Red Punch
Aspect: 1 Hurt
Description: Channel the Hurt aspect in a specific way through your fists, forearms, and elbows to make your punches twice as efficient and damaging against creatures.

Name: Red Kick
Aspect: 1 Hurt
Description: Channel the Hurt aspect in a specific way through your feet, shins, and knees to make your kicks twice as efficient and damaging against creatures.

You've learned a new martial technique!

Name: Vulnerability
Aspect: 1 Hurt + 1 Destruction
Description: Push some of the magic into your target while attacking. The place you push it into will be temporarily weakened and more vulnerable against subsequent attacks to this area, especially if you are using the Hurt aspect as part of the attack.

You've learned a new martial technique!

Name: Red Skin
Aspect: 1 Hurt + 1 Protection
Description: Channel magic through your skin in a specific way. Your skin will appear slightly redder. When a creature attacks you using their body parts, those body parts will suffer twice as much of natural blowback, making it more painful to punch or kick, or otherwise attack you without a weapon.

You've learned a new martial technique!

Name: Red Mist
Aspect: 1 Hurt + 1 Mind
Description: This technique makes your sweat evaporate and linger around your body as a barely visible red-tinted aura of steam. When opponents touch the steam, the area touched gets amplified pain sensations. If they feel pain in the place of contact, it becomes worse.

You've learned a new martial technique!

Name: Internal Trauma
Aspect: 1 Hurt + 1 Water
Description: At the moment of attack, infuse your hit with magic, making most of the force of your attack transfer as vibrations and spikes of pressure in blood vessels in the area where the attack lands.

You've learned a new martial technique!

Name: Red Echo
Aspect: 1 Hurt + 1 Air
Description: Channel Hurt through your breath and voice. When you shout or exhale sharply, the sound carries a minor Hurt effect - causing brief, sharp pain in the ears and sinuses of anyone within close range. The effect is disorienting but not damaging.

You've learned a new martial technique!

Name: Red Shadow
Aspect: 2 Hurt + 1 Semblance
Description: Channel Hurt through your movements. Afterimages of your attacks linger in the air for a moment - a faint red glow that pulses with violet. Anyone struck by the afterimage, which then fades quickly, experiences a brief but intense burst of pain, as if they had been hit. More advanced usage can create these afterimages for a multitude of attacks at once.

You've learned a new martial technique!

Name: Shrug It Off
Aspect: 2 Protection + 1 Hurt + 1 Aether
Description: A more unorthodox technique, usually used in bursts. It temporarily turns off the feeling of pain and reduces damage to half, but only if the user takes the hit on purpose. Perfect for moments, when one wants to trade the hits.

You've learned a new martial technique!

Name: Pain Transfer
Aspect: 3 Hurt + 1 Life
Description: Transfer part of your current sensation of pain with each landed strike. It causes a sudden spike of pain and discomfort in the hit area of the target briefly, at the same time slightly reducing the pain of the user for a moment.

You've learned a new martial technique!

Name: Bloody Feast
Aspect: 3 Hurt + 2 Healing
Description: This technique causes spilled blood from the enemy that lands on and stains you to be consumed and transformed into a slight burst of healing and invigoration for the user.

You've learned a new martial technique!

Name: Burning Blood
Aspect: 2 Hurt + 1 Fire + 1 Life
Description: This technique causes your own spilled blood, which lands on and sticks to the enemy, to suddenly become boiling hot and catch fire. It evaporates in the process, leaving burns on the enemy's body.

You've learned a new martial technique!

Name: Blood Echo
Aspect: 2 Hurt + 1 Mind + 1 Semblance
Description: This technique causes a lingering imprint of your spilled blood to remain in the area. Anyone who steps into the blood later experiences a brief but intense phantom pain - as if they have stepped into a memory of violence or shard of glass.

You've learned a new martial technique!

Name: Bone Snapping
Aspect: 1 Hurt + 1 Earth
Description: At the moment of attack, infuse your hit with magic, making most of the force of your attack transfer directly into the nearby bones in the area, instead of being diffused through surrounding tissues.

You've learned a new martial technique!

Name: Butchery
Aspect: 3 Hurt + 1 Metal
Description: This technique is channeled through the sharp edge of a weapon or tool. It makes it unusually efficient at cutting soft, unprotected tissues of the target. Even a relatively dulled edge can be dangerous with this technique. Doesn’t affect bones.

You've learned a new martial technique!

Name: Lunge
Aspect: 1 Transformation
Description: This sword technique allows the user to lengthen their blade for a moment in a burst of motion when performing a lunging attack (up to 4 inches). It gives an unexpected burst of reach for the attack.

You've learned a new martial technique!

Name: Shield Breaking
Aspect: 3 Metal + 1 Destruction
Description: This simple sword technique, used at the moment of attack, makes the blade more efficient at deforming and cutting metal.

You've learned a new martial technique!

Name: Armor Piercing
Aspect: 2 Metal + 1 Force + 1 Transformation
Description: This technique is channeled through the tip of a weapon. At the moment of impact, the tip briefly becomes harder and more pointed, allowing it to pierce through armor that would otherwise deflect it. The effect is momentary - just long enough to penetrate.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Karmic Retribution
Aspect: 4 Aether + 2 Hurt + 1 Lore + 1 Destruction
Description: This spell is a kind of aura that can be channeled into your weapons or even some solid magical projectiles. It causes a poisoning-like effect and great suffering to the target on contact, but proportional to how much they have hurt others. It essentially turns the pain they dealt to others against themselves, converting it into "soul decay" damage, which affects the shape of the soul and causes the body to take damage as well. The spell sees the older caused pain worse, not counting it completely.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Tree Birth
Aspect: 3 Wood + 3 Creation + 2 Life + 1 Transformation
Description: This spell requires a piece of wood (at least acorn-sized) to infuse. After this is done, the piece of wood will transform and sprout into a healthy sapling of the tree from which the wood was taken.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Seed of Renewal
Aspect: 2 Wood + 2 Life + 1 Creation
Description: A simpler variant of Tree Birth that can be cast on a single living seed, causing it to sprout and grow into a healthy sapling over the course of a few hours. It does not require wood - only a viable seed.

You've learned a new ritual!

Name: Forest Awakening
Aspect: 4 Wood + 3 Life + 2 Creation + 1 Transformation + 1 Earth
Description: A large ritual that can sprout an entire grove from fallen wood. It requires a piece of wood from each tree and a decent amount of time and energy to perform. The result is a new forest, growing from the remnants of the old.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Seed Duplication
Aspect: 2 Life + 2 Creation + 1 Transformation
Description: This spell targets a single or a few plant seeds. The target goes through a process that visibly resembles cell division, creating two seeds of the same type. However, the created seeds are not clones of the original, but rather the same species with a bit of genetic variation.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Wood Petrification
Aspect: 2 Transformation + 1 Wood + 1 Earth
Description: This spell is used on a volume of wood to gradually turn it into petrified wood. The larger the volume, the longer it takes. There is a maximum volume of a target (around 17 cubic meters). Allows the caster to petrify only specific parts of a wooden object - such as the outer layer, or a decorative pattern.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Wood Hardening
Aspect: 2 Transformation + 1 Wood + 1 Force
Description: A spell inspired by Wood Petrification that hardens wood without turning it to stone. The wood becomes denser, more durable, and resistant to damage, but retains its organic nature. Useful for tools, weapons, and structural elements. Beware, it becomes heavier and might sink.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Coal Making
Aspect: 2 Transformation + 1 Wood + 1 Fire
Description: This spell is used on a volume of wood to gradually turn it into charcoal of that type of wood. It works more quickly on many smaller chunks of wood than on one large piece. The larger the volume, the longer it takes. There is a maximum volume of a target (around 1.72 cubic meters).

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Wood Drying
Aspect: 3 Wood + 1 Air + 1 Water
Description: This spell is used on a volume of wood to gradually and quickly dry it, making the material ready for construction uses. The process doesn’t damage wood. The larger the volume, the longer it takes. There is a maximum volume of a target (around 2.33 cubic meters).

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Wood Bending
Aspect: 2 Wood + 1 Water
Description: This spell is used on a volume of wood to make it bend as if it had been steamed, and then harden it into its new, changed shape. The larger the volume, the longer it takes. There is a maximum volume of a target (around 0.345 cubic meters).

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Wood Glue
Aspect: 2 Wood + 1 Water + 1 Order
Description: This spell fuses two pieces of wood together at their contact surfaces, creating a bond as strong as the surrounding wood. The wood must be clean and dry, and the pieces must be held together during the process. Useful for joinery and repair.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Rust Removal
Aspect: 3 Metal + 1 Air + 1 Chaos
Description: This spell produces a cone or ray area of effect (which feels and looks like wind) that separates and grinds rust away, leaving behind a clear metallic surface. It specializes in iron alloys, but can be tuned to work on some other metals.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Iron Destressing
Aspect: 3 Metal + 1 Fire + 1 Order
Description: This spell is used on a volume of metal (or part of it) and lessens its mechanical fatigue, dealing with microscopic damage to the structure of the metal. It specializes in iron alloys, but can be tuned to work on some other metals.

You've learned a new ritual!

Name: Alloy Separation
Aspect: 3 Metal + 3 Transformation + 2 Chaos + 1 Order
Description: This is a small ritual that separates a targeted volume of metal alloy into its component elements. For example, it can separate brass into copper and zinc, or steel into iron and carbon. The process is slow and requires precision. It is less effective and slower on alloys with many components.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Metal Purity Testing
Aspect: 1 Metal + 2 Lore + 1 Light
Description: A divination spell that reveals the purity and composition of a metal sample. The caster perceives the metal as a color or pattern that indicates its components and any impurities. However, the information depends on the user's knowledge. If the alloy contains substances unknown to the user, they will be marked as unknown.

You've learned a new ritual!

Name: Stone Liquefaction
Aspect: 3 Earth + 2 Water + 1 Transformation
Description: This ritual targets a volume of stone (up to 54.3 cubic meters) and turns it into a liquid similar to cement, but textured like the targeted stone. Different liquefied stones cannot mix. This "cement" will set over time and turn back into the original stone. Denser kinds of rock create heavier, less fluid "cement" and harden back more quickly.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Stone Molding
Aspect: 2 Earth + 1 Water + 1 Order
Description: A less powerful variant of Stone Liquefaction turned into a spell form that softens stone to a clay-like consistency without fully liquefying it. The stone can be shaped by hand or with tools, then hardens back to its original density. Useful for detailed carving and repair work.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Stone Fusion
Aspect: 3 Earth + 1 Fire + 1 Order
Description: A spell that fuses two pieces of stone together at their contact surfaces, creating a seamless bond. The stone at the interface briefly softens, then hardens into a continuous mass. Used for joining stone elements without mortar.

You've learned a new ritual!

Name: Summon the Dead
Aspect: 6 Aether + 4 Lore + 4 Death + 1 Alien + 1 Chaos
Description: This unique and unusual work of magic allows you to summon echoes of the dead - something like ghosts. It works best on the recently dead or preserved corpses, and using it repeatedly on the same place makes the spell work less effectively.

Unfortunately, you probably won't be able to interrogate anything useful from the echo of the dead. They are happy, blissful, and usually talk about good things, or simply sing. They are incapable of suffering. Weird.

You've learned a new ritual!

Name: Summon Imp
Aspect: 2 Alien + 1 Fire + 1 Hurt
Description: Summon and trap a weak creature from some hellish dimension to bind it to serve you in exchange for something or by force. They are varied, and an experienced practitioner might find a specific kind of imp they desire for the job. Dead imps leave behind almost no physical traces. They are as smart as a human toddler, but cunning in certain areas, and different imps have different talents.

You've learned a new ritual!

Name: Lesser Flame Summoning
Aspect: 2 Alien + 2 Flame + 1 Aether
Description: Summon a lesser spirit of fire to perform a task or bind it to your service. They do not have a mind of their own beyond what the summoner gives them. They have a strange way of thinking. Such a spirit might be used to power a large lantern or be settled into a furnace. In certain circumstances, it is possible for a lesser spirit to grow or become unstable, but this usually does not happen.

You've learned a new ritual!

Name: Bring Helping Hands
Aspect: 2 Alien + 1 Semblance + 1 Mind + 1 Force
Description: Use a ritual to obtain or discard this capability. You can summon ghost-like hands from the realm of palms. They can perform simple tasks requiring dexterity. They are much better at their job if you know how to do what you ask of them using your own hands - they partially draw on your understanding and skills.

They cannot stay too far from you for too long, or the summoning will break (after about half an hour, give or take). You can summon two, four, six, eight, ten, or a dozen hands, and assign and reassign tasks to and between individual hands.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Fire Shield
Aspect: 2 Protection + 1 Fire
Description: This spell can be cast on the self, another creature, or an object. It creates an invisible aura that becomes more visible proportionally to how much heat is trying to breach it. The aura blocks excessive heat, preventing it from reaching the target. However, if too much heat affects it at once, or if it is strained for too long, the shield may "pop" and leave the target defenseless.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Shroud from Flame
Aspect: 1 Protection + 1 Fire
Description: This spell can be cast on the self, another creature, or an object. It creates a kind of field that penetrates the target's volume, reducing how much excess heat it receives from external sources and making it more resistant to the effects of heat. However, it does not block it completely - it just severely reduces the detrimental effects. For example, instead of receiving third-degree burns in two seconds, one will receive first-degree burns over the course of twenty seconds.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Flaming Armor
Aspect: 1 Protection + 2 Flame
Description: This spell can be cast on the self or another creature. It produces a barely visible effect that resembles a heat wave in the air. It will produce bursts of flame and heat when something violently tries to pierce it, or at the user's will. This will scorch the attacker, parry and burn projectiles, and more. 

This armor can be weakened and turned off by too much offense, but it will return if given a breathing room. As a side effect, it keeps the user comfortably warm even in an intense cold and provides resistance against effects that impose cold or steal heat.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Protection
Aspect: 1 Protection
Description: This spell creates an invisible force field that briefly flickers silver when hit. When something connects with this field, 98.7% of its force is perfectly reflected back. However, if the field is hit with force above a certain limit, or too often within a period of time, it will pop - deflecting things in the process but going on cooldown. 

The cooldown is proportional to the attack that broke it (from a few seconds to a minute). It can only be cast on the caster. An experienced user can layer up to three fields. It is bad at protecting against things like heat, poison gas, or electrical discharge (although it still protects a bit).

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Force Shield
Aspect: 2 Semblance + 1 Protection + 1 Force
Description: This spell creates a semi-transparent, orange-tinted force field that acts as a handheld shield, with an incredible ability to partially negate, absorb, and deflect force used against it. Can be turned off/on without dispelling.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Reinforcement
Aspect: 1 Protection
Description: This spell is channeled through the caster or items in contact with them, making targets more resistant to damage and physical effects, but only slightly (1 to 30% more). It works against a great variety of mundane phenomena, better against some and worse against others.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Deflection Field
Aspect: 2 Protection + 1 Air
Description: This spell creates a subtle, invisible field around the caster that gently deflects incoming projectiles (arrows, bolts, and small thrown objects) slightly off course. The deflection is not perfect; it causes the projectile to miss by a few inches rather than stopping it entirely. Fast-moving or extremely heavy projectiles are less affected. The field lasts for several minutes or until the caster is struck by a hit that exceeds its capacity.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Thermal Insulation
Aspect: 2 Protection + 1 Fire + 1 Water
Description: This spell creates a protective layer around the caster that resists extreme temperatures - both heat and cold. It does not block damage entirely, but significantly reduces the effects of environmental temperature extremes and temperature-based attacks. A person wearing this spell could walk through a burning building or a freezing blizzard with only minor discomfort. The effect lasts for up to an hour.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Shock Absorber
Aspect: 2 Protection + 1 Force
Description: This spell creates a subtle, invisible cushion around the caster that absorbs the force of impacts: falls, blunt strikes, and explosive shockwaves. The cushion reduces the effective force of any impact by half, but each absorbed impact weakens the spell. After absorbing a certain amount of total force, the spell dissipates and must be recast. Can be overwhelmed.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Reactive Plating
Aspect: 2 Protection + 1 Metal + 1 Force
Description: This spell coats the caster's skin or armor in a barely visible metallic sheen. When struck, the coating momentarily hardens and disperses the force of the blow across a wider area, reducing the damage significantly. The coating is most effective against blunt force and slashing attacks, but offers little protection against piercing attacks or energy-based damage. The effect lasts up to 11 minutes.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Lingering Ward
Aspect: 2 Protection + 1 Time + 1 Order
Description: This spell is cast on a location or object (a door, a chest, or a perimeter) rather than on a person. It creates a protective field that lasts for hours or days, absorbing or deflecting attacks against the warded object. 

The ward is not as strong as a personal shield, but it persists without the caster's attention. It can be set to trigger on specific conditions (e.g., "only if touched by a living creature"). The ward fades when its stored energy is depleted.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Ward of Negation
Aspect: 4 Protection + 2 Order + 1 Aether + 1 Essence
Description: This spell creates a shimmering, silvery bubble-like field around the caster that actively negates magical effects that target them. A curse aimed at the caster will be weakened or dispelled entirely. A scrying spell will fail to penetrate the ward. A direct magical attack will be reduced in power or slightly thrown off course. The ward is not perfect (powerful, cunning or specialized magic can overwhelm it) but it provides a significant defense against hostile magic. The effect has to be actively sustained. Stationary.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Phalanx Ward
Aspect: 3 Protection + 1 Force + 1 Order
Description: This spell creates a large, semi-transparent shield in front of the caster that can cover multiple people. The shield is rectangular and about the size of a tower shield. It blocks physical projectiles and absorbs kinetic force, but it must be actively maintained - the caster must hold the shield in place. It can withstand a significant amount of force before breaking, but it does not protect against attacks from the sides or rear.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Adaptive Shell
Aspect: 2 Protection + 1 Lore + 1 Transformation
Description: This spell creates a protective shell around the caster that adapts to the type of attack it faces. When struck by fire, the shell becomes fire-resistant. When struck by a blade, it hardens. When struck by a curse, it becomes resistant to magic. The adaptation is not instant (it takes a few hits to fully adjust) and the shell can only adapt to one or two damage types at a time. The effect lasts for 17 minutes.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Flaming Droplet
Aspect: 1 Fire
Description: This spell creates and throws a ball-like projectile made of fire. It is round, up to 44 cm in size, and really bouncy. Each bounce leaves behind a flaming puddle, like burning napalm. Each bounce makes the projectile smaller.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Fire Ball
Aspect: 1 Fire
Description: This spell creates a ball of flame and shoots it. The orb is around 30 cm in diameter and suddenly expands into a cloud of flame on impact, like burning gas exploding. Classic.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Fire Orb
Aspect: 1 Fire
Description: This creates a smooth projectile of yellow, swirling flame. It is like a smooth marble, almost looking solid. On impact, it turns into a great number of extremely hot and quick white sparks flying in all directions, which slightly penetrate and burn things on contact.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Burning Sphere
Aspect: 1 Fire
Description: This spell creates a small, bubble-like projectile as small as a fist, filled with orange fire. Many bubbles can be created quickly. The projectile is heavy and very hot; it rams into and melts things on contact, getting smaller over time or from burning through things.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Smoldering Touch
Aspect: 1 Fire
Description: This spell causes the caster's hands to become hot enough to ignite flammable materials on contact. The heat is contained to the hands and does not harm the caster. Useful for starting fires, lighting torches, or leaving burning handprints.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Miniature Sun
Aspect: 1 Fire + 1 Light
Description: This spell creates a small, glowing orb of white light and shoots it at extreme speed. On impact, it destabilizes over a few moments (enough time for it to melt through many things) and then violently explodes, practically evaporating everything in a small radius.

You've learned a new martial technique!

Name: Solar Prominence
Aspect: 1 Fire + 1 Light
Description: This martial technique allows the user to create and partially control the shape of bright loops of plasma extending from their body. Good for melee attacks or to evaporate incoming projectiles.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Flashfire
Aspect: 1 Fire + 2 Light
Description: This spell creates a blinding flash of white light accompanied by a wave of intense heat. The flash temporarily (or not) blinds anyone within 10 meters who is looking in the direction of the spell. The heat is enough to ignite flammable materials and cause first-degree burns on exposed skin. The effect is brief: a single, directional burst.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Solar Blade
Aspect: 2 Fire + 1 Light + 1 Sembalance
Description: This spell creates a blade of condensed plasma and light extending from the caster's hand - a sword made of solar energy. The blade is incredibly hot and can cut through most materials. It lasts for a few minutes and can be dismissed at will. The blade sheds bright light, illuminating the area around the caster.

You've learned a new crafting ritual!

Name: Amber Glass Casting
Aspect: 2 Wood + 1 Light
Description: This small ritual allows one to transform wood into an amber-like substance that can be used like glass. The ritual works best on sawdust. Different types of wood produce different hues of "amber glass," and some types are objectively better to use for the ritual.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Mud Brick Shaping
Aspect: 4 Earth + 1 Order
Description: This spell is cast on loose soil, mud, or clay. It quickly shapes a small volume of material into robust mud bricks (or several). The caster can tune the size and proportions of the bricks a bit.

You've learned a new crafting ritual!

Name: Wooden Glue
Aspect: 3 Wood + 1 Water + 1 Earth
Description: This little ritual allows one to turn wood into a liquid resin-like substance, which hardens over time or at the user's will into a hard amber-like form (not as hard or clear as amber glass). It is very sticky and makes great glue while fluid.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Screw Spell
Aspect: 3 Force + 1 Order
Description: This spell targets small objects. It can apply rotation and push/pull to them. Basically, it works as a great substitute for a screwdriver - great for screwing in or unscrewing bolts\ and other fasteners.

You've learned a new ritual!

Name: Quicklime Transmutation
Aspect: 2 Earth + 1 Fire + 1 Transformation
Description: This small ritual transforms limestone or shells into quicklime, a key ingredient for mortar, plaster, and tanning. The process is quick and efficient, producing usable quicklime in minutes rather than days.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Rope Weave
Aspect: 2 Wood + 1 Force + 1 Semblance
Description: This spell transforms plant fibers (grass, bark, or reeds) into strong, flexible rope. The rope can be made in any length up to 9.8 meters at a time (although, you can continue from where you finished last time) and can be tuned for thickness and strength. Some fibers are obviously better than others to use.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Torch
Aspect: 2 Fire + 1 Wood
Description: This spell produces flame on one end of a stick or small piece of wood the caster wields. The flame keeps burning on the top and is very hard to put out while the spell is working. The stick itself slowly turns into burnt wood, consumed in the process of sustaining the flame at the top. The user can turn the flame on or off at any moment, or control the intensity of the fire.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Water Soap
Aspect: 7 Water + 1 Purity
Description: This spell makes a small amount of targeted water act soapy: it produces foam and bubbles and is good at cleaning things. After the spell is stopped, or after some time has passed, the water returns to its normal state.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Water Probe
Aspect: 9 Water + 1 Lore
Description: This spell targets a volume of water. It gives the caster general information about how much the liquid is contaminated, indicated on a scale from blue to red. It does not reveal the specific nature of the contamination - only how far it is from the purity of distilled water.

You've learned a new spell!

Name: Disinfection
Aspect: 9 Spirit + 1 Death + 1 Purity
Description: This spell produces a small amount of temporary liquid with a slightly gelatinous consistency that smells like alcohol. It is a great disinfectant and good at loosing the stains to be removed.

You've learned a new crafting ritual!

Name: Iron Wood Production
Aspect: 4 Wood + 2 Iron + 1 Transformation + 1 Essence
Description: This is a crafting ritual. You need a piece of hard wood and a tiny amount of iron. Name: Spell-Arrester Copper Forging
Aspect: 5 Metal + 2 Essence + 1 Transformation + 1 Air + 2 Lighting

Description: This is a complex alchemical ritual that processes raw cesium into a stable, magical metal known as blightinite. You gain the ability, knowledge, and skill to overcharge your spells. This allows you to put more "power" into any work of magic to intensify its effect or increase its scale (within certain limits). Limitations and unique interactions vary between spells. Some spells may even offer multiple ways to overcharge them. However, overcharged spells are usually less stable and more prone to miscasting, as well as harder to wield with accuracy.

You gain the ability, knowledge, and skill to undercharge your spells. This allows you to still use a spell while spending fewer resources on it (reducing its cost). In exchange, the spell becomes proportionally less intense, scales down, or loses some of its properties.

There are limits to how far a spell can be undercharged, and certain spells react differently than others to this trick. Sometimes undercharging may be impossible or even dangerous for specific types of magic. However, it can be a good way to save resources in a moment of need.

You gain the ability, knowledge, and skill to cast two spells at the same time. You can run them in parallel - whether the same spell or two different ones. This makes the overall cost slightly higher, but it can be quite useful. This perk only affects active casting; sustained effects can run in parallel on their own.

This is an upgrade to Dual Casting, refining your methodology and multitasking abilities when working with magic. It lets you execute three spells in parallel with only a slight increase in overall cost.

>Requires Dual Casting

This is nigh perfected methodology, natural talent, and skill derived from Dual and Triple Casting. You can juggle multiple magical works at once in parallel with only a slight increase in overall cost. How many you can cast simultaneously, and how safe and depended it is, depends on the nature of the spells in question. 

>Requires Triple Casting

This perk grants you the knowledge, skill, and ability to prepare multiple spells for execution and then cast them all at once. You can begin preparing the first spell while keeping it from actually executing, then add another, and another...

How many spells you can chain together depends on the nature of the spells, your focus, skill, and talent. Maintaining spells in suspension carries a cost and cannot be done forever - only for a few tens of minutes at most.

The overall cost when executing the chain is slightly higher than casting them separately. You can also withdraw and break the chain before execution, which removes all suspended spells at once with no significant cost. When the chain is ready, you execute the spells in order, almost simultaneously.

You can spend time to convert a work of magic into a matrix of sorts and create a temporary slot for it in your soul. The process has an associated cost, but it mostly just takes a lot of time (from several minutes to a full day).

A spell placed in a slot is suspended at no ongoing cost and can be instantly executed by you at any time. However, it cannot be modified in any way. The only way to free the slot is either to cast the spell or to take just as long to unravel it from the slot.

You can prepare several slots this way. How many depends on the nature of the spells you place in them, but typically you can maintain between one and seven slots at once.

>Requires Chain Casting

This methodology lets you "rush" spells and some other works of magic to execute them faster by skipping certain steps, using mnemonic tricks, and performing several parts of a single magical work at once. How much you can rush a spell depends on its nature: some spells cannot be quick-executed at all.

Spells cast this way are riskier and more prone to miscasting. Their intensity may also be either reduced or increased unpredictably. The main drawback is the inconsistency of these side effects, though the general nature of the spell is always preserved.

You can change the cosmetic effects of your spells, if they have any. You can make them sound or look different, but not in a way that alters their general behavior. Not all spells can be affected, though most can accept some aesthetic adjustments. It costs you virtually nothing to make a charm's ray pink instead of red. This does not affect more esoteric or detailed methods of observing spells.

This is an upgrade to Cosmetic Calibration. It lets you make your spells less noticeable - including reducing their "loudness" for magic detection and analysis. You can also introduce noise or more profound changes to a spell's perceptible effects to confuse and mislead observers.

However, you still cannot change the general nature of the work. An observer may still tell that you are casting some sort of curse, but it will be much harder to identify the specifics. It introduces cost growth proportional to degree and complexety of changes.

>Requires Cosmetic Calibration

This is the near-perfected methodology of Subtle Spellwork and Cosmetic Calibration. It allows you to conceal or almost completely remove any visible effects of a magical work: no light rays, visible projectiles, odd smells... Almost nothing.

The spell can still be detected by more specialized observation and sensing methods, and the "carry" of the spell remains - it's just harder to perceive. There is still a ray, but it's invisible. Some spells cannot be hidden this way due to their inherent nature.

>Requires Subtle Spellwork

This method lets you "stretch" a spell, extending its duration while sacrificing some of its intensity. This can be applied in two ways. To the effect: the spell's effect becomes weaker, but lasts longer. To the carrier: A short-lived ray becomes a continuous one by reducing the intensity of the effect per unit of time. Overall cost increased only slightly. Not all spells can be stretched this way.

This method lets you shorten the duration of a spell's effect while increasing its intensity in the moment. It interacts with the spell's carrier in various ways - details you'll need to discover on your own.

This technique is applied to the spell's effect, but the carrier is always affected as well. Some spell's carrier may become quicker but more short-lived, losing their maximum range. For continuous works of magic, the intensified effect may become less stable over time. However, in the moment, intensity increases significantly while the cost rises only slightly to moderately.

This perk grants you the skill, knowledge, and ability to interrupt spells mid-execution while recovering part of their cost. It also allows you to un-conjure certain things from the Transformation chapter and regain some of the cost, as well as stop a ritual before completion while retaining some of the cost not yet used in the effect. It never gives you back the whole cost, but even third is great in certain situations and sometimes there is a need to stop magic suddenly.

This perk grants you the skill, knowledge, and ability to fluidly and continuously transition from one spell into another without interrupting the overall process, assuming the spells are similar enough in nature.

For example, transitioning from a spell that produces a cone of flame into one that creates a ray of fire is quite easy, with almost no increase in cost. This allows you to gradually morph one spell into another in the process of continuous execution.

You have the skill, knowledge, and ability to sacrifice some of a spell's intensity or prolong its execution time in exchange for producing multiple copies of the same effect at once. For example, firing four rays of a curse instead of one, but each is weaker or taking longer to execute them together. Not all spells can be used this way, and there is a limit to how many copies you can create. The more copies you attempt, the faster the cost grows.

By incorporating ritualistic aspects into your works of magic (such as specific gestures and signs, words, or even entire poems) you can increase the scale, intensity, and longevity of magical works to varying degrees. The kind of ritualistic aspects you use will slightly affect the spell and even change how it interacts with other metamagic options (for better or worse). 

Multiple ritualistic elements can be combined on a single spell to enhance it further. One spell can be affected using different ritualistic parts for various degrees of effect.With this, you can effectively pay with execution time and ritual performance to improve a spell without side effects. However, this approach may be unwieldy in certain situations.

This perk grants you the skill and knowledge to pre-program certain simple changes to a spell's carrier trajectory before casting, or to give it a slight nudge while it is already active with some focus. It increases accuracy and allows techniques such as curving spells or changing their speed mid-flight. It cannot be too complicated and the cost grows proportionally to degree and complexity of changes, depending partially on the nature of the work too.

Entering a specific state of mind or experiencing certain emotions can affect spells whose nature resonates with that feeling. This works especially well for many spells from the Curses and Blessings chapters, for instance.

Using certain tricks and techniques, you can forcefully enter a specific state of mind or evoke a particular emotion, then use that state to influence your magical work: enhancing it, slightly warping its effect, or in some cases causing it to fail or rarely even miscast. This skill is not easy to execute and carries certain psychological risks.

You can generate and control small amounts of Metallic Fire: orbs, wisps, and sparks of heavy, glinting flame colored gray, copper and patina. You also possess the skill to craft small magitech devices and enchanted trinkets that can produce this flame autonomously using appropriate fuel or energy source. The flame naturally exists between 800-1600°C. Below that, it extinguishes; above, it collapses into mundane fire.

The fire does not physically turn things to metal. Instead, it infuses materials with conceptual metallic traits while they interact with it. The effect depends on application:

1. Burning (best): Ash and smoke retain strong, permanent metallic properties - excellent for reagents or crafting.
2. Catalyzing (decent): Cooking, brewing, or firing clay imparts lasting but lesser metallic traits to the finished product.
3. State-changing (worst): Melting or boiling creates dramatic effects only while the material remains in that state; upon cooling, only faint, barely-detectible traces remain.

You can generate and control small amounts of Cooking Fire: orbs, wisps, and sparks of warm yellow-brown flame that faintly smells of fresh bread, caramel, and roasted meat. You also possess the skill to craft small magitech devices and enchanted trinkets that can produce this flame autonomously using appropriate fuel or energy sources. The flame naturally exists between 250–600°C. Below that, it extinguishes; above, it collapses into mundane fire.

The fire does not physically alter composition. Instead, it infuses materials with conceptual traits of Flavor and Nourishment. It even works on non-edible items, but usually not much. The effect depends on application:

1. Catalyzing (best): Cooking, brewing, or baking imparts rich, lasting flavor and enhanced nutritional value to the finished product.
2. Burning (worst): Complete combustion yields ash and smoke with faint nourishing properties - slightly better fertilizer for plants, but little else.
3. State-changing (nonfunctional): Melting or boiling produces no meaningful effect.
